summary: The PCs' post: the Wasp Marshals for the southeast, overseeing all Wasp bounty hunting in six domains (Fox, Sparrow, Kakita, Etsuko, Reiji, Daika) and reporting to Tsuruchi Kyoma a few times a week. They guide the Inspectors, may investigate personally, and receive official guests. The PCs are of the upper 7th rank, the Inspectors of the lower 7th. They replaced Tsuruchi Kaminari, Tsuruchi Danji and Tsuruchi Okihito, promoted in 1130 to be Marshals in the Yasuki Estates.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Wasp hierarchy

summary: The Wasp officer assigned to each of the six domains under the Marshals (the PCs), one per domain, of the lower 7th rank, each with a small team of Escorts. Not to be confused with a tariff inspector at a city gate.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Wasp hierarchy

summary: Members of an Inspector's small team who help collect bounties and deliver the fugitive (or head) to wherever the bounty was placed to claim the reward. Tsuruchi Hideki is an Escort.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Wasp hierarchy

summary: The chain of command for Wasp bounty hunting in the southeast: Tsuruchi Kyoma, then the PCs as Marshals (haribugyo), then one Inspector (metsuke) per domain, then each Inspector's Escorts (gosonin). The campaign wiki page has the org chart.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Wasp hierarchy

term: Distinguished Plenipotentiary to the Southern Allies
summary: Tsuruchi Kyoma's title: the Wasp envoy overseeing bounty operations among the Wasp's southern allies (the Three Man Alliance). He keeps residences in Shinden Kitsune and Shiro Suzume; the PCs run his office while household stewards run his homes.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Wasp Clan NPCs > Tsuruchi Byakuya

summary: The PCs' boss: Distinguished Plenipotentiary to the Southern Allies of the Wasp, a close friend of the Wasp daimyo Tsuruchi, overseeing bounty work among the southern allies while focusing on cementing the Three Man Alliance through long nights of shared cups. Born Kyo Kyoma of the Kyo house; at the 1110 banquet he killed Kyo Fumikazu, who was about to stab Tsuruchi in the back. Husband of Tsuruchi Hitomi.
related: Distinguished Plenipotentiary to the Southern Allies

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign

summary: One of the three previous Marshals whom the PCs replaced; promoted at the start of 1130 to be a Marshal in the Yasuki Estates.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Wasp hierarchy

summary: One of the three previous Marshals whom the PCs replaced; promoted at the start of 1130 to be a Marshal in the Yasuki Estates.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Wasp hierarchy

summary: One of the three previous Marshals whom the PCs replaced; promoted at the start of 1130 to be a Marshal in the Yasuki Estates.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Wasp hierarchy

summary: One of the six domains the PCs oversee as Marshals: the Fox Clan's lands around the Kitsune Mori; capital Shinden Kitsune. Wasp Inspector: Tsuruchi Jirou. Imperial magistrate: Seppun Gorou.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Wasp hierarchy

summary: One of the six domains the PCs oversee as Marshals: the Sparrow Clan's hills; capital Shiro Suzume. Wasp Inspector: Tsuruchi Riku. Imperial magistrate: Seppun Gisako.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Wasp hierarchy

summary: One of the six domains the PCs oversee as Marshals: the ruling house of the Kakita Family of the Crane Clan; capital Kyuden Kakita. Wasp Inspector: Tsuruchi Kinji. Imperial magistrate: Seppun Shogo.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Wasp hierarchy

summary: One of the six domains the PCs oversee as Marshals: the northernmost Daidoji domain of the Crane Clan; capital Shiro Etsuko. Wasp Inspector: Tsuruchi Nobumasa. Imperial magistrate: Otomo Genzo.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Wasp hierarchy

summary: One of the six domains the PCs oversee as Marshals: the northeasternmost Hida domain of the Crab Clan; capital Shiro Reiji. Wasp Inspector: Tsuruchi Fumitake. Imperial magistrate: Seppun Sena.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Wasp hierarchy

summary: One of the six domains the PCs oversee as Marshals: the Bayushi domain of the Scorpion Clan west of the Kitsune forest; capital Shiro Daika. Wasp Inspector: Tsuruchi Fumikazu. Imperial magistrate: Hantei Kairi.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Wasp hierarchy

summary: A tiny minor clan founded about 15 years before the campaign by Tsuruchi, first of his name, with Crane backing; its holdings are the single mountain province of Hachinaga. Its charter lets every Wasp samurai act as an Imperial magistrate to pursue Imperial bounties, which are a large share of its income. Its three lineages are the Tsuruchi, Ami and Kyoma lineages, and its chancellery is "the Crane wives". It leads the Three Man Alliance.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign

summary: The Emperor's charter creating the Wasp Clan (1116). It grants every Wasp samurai the authority to act as an Imperial magistrate for the purpose of pursuing Imperial bounties, so every Wasp is a potential bounty hunter.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Tsuruchi's legacy

summary: Tsuruchi, first of his name: founder and daimyo of the Wasp Clan, born Bayushi no Kyo Tsuruchi of the Shin lineage. After his parents were killed at a banquet in 1110 and the Lion took Hachinaga Keep, he became a ronin Imperial bounty hunter famed for his bow ("A single arrow, a single life"), retook the keep in 1115, executed his treacherous uncle Matsu no Zenji Ginjiro with the broken sword Isshin, and was made daimyo of the new clan in 1116. He carries no sword at home and declared there shall be no Ancestral Sword of the Wasp. Married to Tsuruchi Naomi; their son is Ichiro.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign

term: A single arrow, a single life
summary: Tsuruchi's motto as a bounty hunter, who preferred to strike down fugitives with his bow rather than challenge them to duels.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Tsuruchi's career as an Imperial bounty hunter

summary: The mountainous province that is the whole of the Wasp Clan's holdings, guarding the narrow Hachinaga pass through the Spine of the World Mountains about 150 miles inland. Ruled by the Shin lineage for over a thousand years, first under the Scorpion (Kyo house).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign

summary: The Wasp Clan's seat. The broken blade of the sword Isshin is still embedded in the floor of its great hall, and Wasp samurai (and many guests) rarely carry swords inside it.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Tsuruchi's legacy

summary: The ancestral sword of the Shin lineage. Tsuruchi surrendered it to his uncle Ginjiro in 1111, took it back in 1115 and snapped it in the floor of Hachinaga Keep's great hall, executing Ginjiro with the broken shard. The blade stays in the floor; the hilt is on an ancestral shrine in the same room.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Tsuruchi's revenge

summary: The lineage descended from Bayushi Shin that ruled Hachinaga province for a thousand years as part of the Scorpion's Kyo house; Tsuruchi's birth lineage and the core of the Wasp's Tsuruchi lineage.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign

summary: A vassal house of the Bayushi Family (Scorpion Clan), daimyo Bayushi no Kyo Haruka. Tsuruchi and Tsuruchi Kyoma were both originally of the Kyo; the Shin lineage once served it.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign

summary: A vassal house of the Matsu Family (Lion Clan) bordering Wasp lands to the north; daimyo Matsu no Zenji Kana. Tsuruchi's mother Natsu was a Zenji, and the Zenji took Hachinaga Keep in 1111.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign

summary: The Wasp lineage made up mostly of the original Shin lineage plus other former Scorpion who joined the Wasp; headed on the chancellery by Tsuruchi Naomi.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Crane Wives

summary: The Wasp's "peasantborn" lineage: mostly the peasant yoriki who helped Tsuruchi as a bounty hunter and the mercenaries who retook Hachinaga Keep, raised to the samurai caste. Headed by Tsuruchi Ami, wife of Tsuruchi Takuan.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Crane Wives > The wives

summary: The Wasp lineage joined by nearly all the samurai from other clans (and many ronin) who came to the Wasp after its founding; the least cohesive of the three. Headed by Tsuruchi Hitomi, Tsuruchi Kyoma's wife.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Crane Wives > The wives

summary: The Wasp Clan chancellery: three Crane courtiers given as wives to Tsuruchi and his two most loyal retainers - Tsuruchi Naomi (Tsuruchi lineage), Tsuruchi Ami (Ami lineage) and Tsuruchi Hitomi (Kyoma lineage). The name alludes to the fable of the crane wife.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Crane Wives

summary: Tsuruchi's wife, youngest daughter of the Crane Champion Doji Kuwanen, one of the Crane wives and head of the Tsuruchi lineage. In 1130 she began matchmaking for their 12-year-old son Ichiro.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Crane Wives > Tsuruchi Naomi

summary: Chancellor of the Ami ("peasantborn") lineage, one of the Crane wives, born Doji no Tsume Ami; wife of Tsuruchi Takuan.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Crane Wives > Tsuruchi Ami

summary: Tsuruchi Kyoma's wife, one of the Crane wives and head of the Kyoma lineage; born a Kakita. Her brother Kakita Daini died losing the ink-flight (Akechi) scrolls to Matsu Agetoki in a wager, and she took the name Hitomi pledging to reclaim them.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Crane Wives > Tsuruchi Hitomi

summary: Silk hangings of calligraphy painted with ink-dipped arrows by the archer-poet Kakita Akechi. Lost by Kakita Daini to Matsu no Masao Agetoki in an archery wager twenty years ago.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Crane Wives > Tsuruchi Hitomi

summary: Wasp Minister of Retainers, Tsuruchi's most accomplished peasant informant from his bounty hunting days and the only peasantborn Wasp to merit a Crane wife (Tsuruchi Ami).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Crane Wives > Tsuruchi Ami

summary: The 12-year-old eldest son of Tsuruchi and Tsuruchi Naomi, heir to the Wasp, who plans to take the name Tsuruchi Ichiro at his gempukku.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Crane Wives > Tsuruchi Naomi

summary: Household steward running Tsuruchi Kyoma's residence in Sparrow lands (Shiro Suzume), an old friend of Kyoma's from the Kyo house, raising his young daughter Hatsuko.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Wasp Clan NPCs > Tsuruchi Byakuya

summary: Steward of Tsuruchi Kyoma's Fox Clan residence; deeply superstitious and a generous patron to the PCs, who gave them charms against fox mischief and amulets for entering the Kitsune Mori.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Wasp Clan NPCs > Tsuruchi Tatsuki

summary: An amulet Tsuruchi Tatsuki gave the PCs for the Kitsune Mori: a small red silk pouch bearing the seal of the Kitsune household sponsoring a journey; carried openly, the wood's fox-spirits leave the bearer alone.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Wasp Clan NPCs > Tsuruchi Tatsuki

summary: An amulet Tsuruchi Tatsuki gave the PCs for the Kitsune Mori: a small brass bell on a staff or pack; while it rings on the path, fox-illusions cannot easily replace the way back.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Wasp Clan NPCs > Tsuruchi Tatsuki

summary: An amulet Tsuruchi Tatsuki gave the PCs for the Kitsune Mori: a small black iron pin worn against the skin, which disrupts low-grade fox glamours.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Wasp Clan NPCs > Tsuruchi Tatsuki

summary: An amulet Tsuruchi Tatsuki gave the PCs for the Kitsune Mori: a small disc of obsidian or smoky quartz worn at the neck that reveals whether a path, hut or face is real.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Wasp Clan NPCs > Tsuruchi Tatsuki

summary: The pact of the three minor clans of the southeast - the Wasp (at its head), the Fox and the Sparrow - formed in 1117: a military defense pact and a voting caucus on the Imperial chancellery, where all three vote together. All three owe favors to the Crane.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Three Man Alliance

summary: Minor clan whose lands ring the Kitsune Mori, descended from ancient shamans and the shapechanging black fox Osusuki; the Kitsune Family. Rich from the forest (lumber, charcoal, white charcoal, incense), with five lineages (the ruling Kitsune plus Toke, Hokke, Saike and Nanke for the four cardinal provinces). Daimyo: Kitsune Ryosei. Wasp ally in the Three Man Alliance.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Fox Clan

summary: The fox forest, third largest in the Empire, bordered by the Lion (north), Scorpion (west), Crane (east) and Crab (south); full of spirits and fox-spirits. The Fox Clan holds it, free of Imperial taxation; it watches outsiders who linger, especially on the Imperial road through Minami province.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Fox Clan > The Kitsune Forest

summary: Fox Clan "shrine-grade" charcoal made from sacred oak, prized for its odorless, almost smokeless burn in shrines and tea ceremonies; overseen by the Fox Ministry of Rites and counterfeited by the bounty target "Kitsune Denhei".

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Fox Clan > The Fox Clan's economy

summary: Minor clan founded by the Crane noble Suzume (the Suzume Family) in the poor Sparrow Hills, where tenant farming is outlawed and Sparrow samurai live in the villages as village overseers sworn to poverty before Daikoku. Poor in rice and coin, they grow tea, mulberry and soybeans. Daimyo: Suzume Mukashino. Wasp ally in the Three Man Alliance.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Sparrow Clan

summary: A Sparrow samurai posted to live in a farming village and manage it in place of a peasant headsman, sworn to a vow of poverty to Daikoku. Found nowhere else in the Empire.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Sparrow Clan > Sparrow land management

summary: A Mantis (Shione family) sugarcane syndicate, said to be founded by smugglers and pirates, with armed outfits throughout this quarter of the Empire.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: The war between the Lion and Crane clans that began in 1122 over Toshi Ranbo; the Three Man Alliance gave the Crane safe passage through Sparrow lands (not Hachinaga pass), and Wasp and Fox samurai helped defend the Sparrow hills.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Three Man Alliance > The Lion/Crane War

summary: A reward registered with an Imperial magistrate for bringing in a fugitive (or a summoned witness); the target is delivered to the magistrate who registered it, who pays out. Traditionally the collector keeps half, their superior takes a tenth, and the rest goes to the daimyo's treasury. Governed by the Doctrine of Three Steps. The campaign wiki explains how bounties work; the Imperial bulletin lists the open ones.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties

summary: The list of outstanding Imperial bounties distributed to local authorities; the campaign wiki keeps the current list (updated as the campaign goes).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: One of the formal gifts around bounties: the small gift given to an Imperial magistrate when registering a bounty.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Registering a bounty

summary: One of the formal gifts around bounties: a gift with no expectation of value, given instead of a token gift when the petitioner already knows the magistrate.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Registering a bounty

summary: One of the formal gifts around bounties: the payment made to the magistrate when a bounty is accepted (a tithe of the bounty), or a gift that funds the bounty itself.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Registering a bounty

summary: One of the formal gifts around bounties: a gift to a local Imperial magistrate who pays out a bounty on someone else's behalf, when the hunter has no prior relationship with them.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Registering a bounty

summary: One of the formal gifts around bounties: a gift recognizing the trouble a request puts a magistrate to, such as forcing an awkward summons.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Registering a bounty

summary: The reward (usually a tithe of the bounty, once collected) paid to an informant who reports a fugitive's whereabouts.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > An example bounty

summary: Bounty target (100 koku): runs an Empire-wide opium cartel, an outstanding duelist who intimidates witnesses, avoids boats for fear of Osano-Wo, travels with Yasuki caravans; summoned by an Imperial magistrate in northern Otaku lands.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (100 koku): Mantis bushi wanted for questioning over the burning of Yasuki sugarcane fields; believed to work for the Silken Syrup Consortium under another name.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (100 koku): an old hermit with long gray hair and a goiter on the right of his neck, who struck Bayushi no Daika Koharu from behind with an axe in the Kitsune forest, accusing him of hunting foxes; travels with disciples.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (100 koku): an unnamed Yasuki smuggler who sails with forged papers and kimono of many clans, his men fighting in the Crab style.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (100 koku): six to eight bandits robbing barges at the oxbow west of Kyuden Kakita, fleeing into Zenji marshes; some carry Crab-style tetsubo.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (75 koku): the bandit lord who robbed the manor of Kakita Hikai, county magistrate of Seitoyama, and should bear a scar from left ear to chin. "Kage" (shadow) is a common bandit alias.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (75 koku): supplied obsidian to the traitor Shinjo Jotsu; scarred stomach and chest, always carries obsidian; seen in Shinden Kitsune.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty (75 koku) posted by the Fox for a branch cut from a sacred humming camphor tree in the Kitsune Forest before Setsubun, probably for a musical instrument; Kakita Ikura the musician left the festival suddenly.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (50 koku): a Mantis man who fled Kyuden Kakita rather than answer Kakita Foruku's duel challenge; seen in Shiro Suzume.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (50 koku): two men and a woman who robbed Daidoji no Etsuko Azami of silk; she splashed the men with indigo dye that stains their hands and nails.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (50 koku): struck a steward and attacked the Witch Hunter Kuni Nakadai at the Sovereign Temple of Hotei in Kyuden Kakita; seen there in pilgrim's clothes.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (50 koku): born Mirumoto Miyuki, exiled from Dragon lands for killing a Shosuro actress, then joined the Togashi Ise Zumi.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (50 koku): eldest daughter of the Fox shugenja Kitsune Shunichi, who accepted Bayushi no Daika Isoshi's duel challenge and then left to "meditate"; the Fox daimyo will not compel her return. She is a PC in the Tuesday group and is not a Wasp.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (40 koku): bandits in the southern Sparrow foothills, raiding northern Daidoji lands; their leader stutters.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty (40 koku) to identify whoever sells counterfeit Kitsune white charcoal in Kakita and Etsuko lands under the name of "Kitsune Denhei", a Fox merchant who does not exist.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (30 koku): tall, thin bandits who rob travelers mid-ford in the Mugi-arai-gawa between Fox and Daidoji lands.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (25 koku): three men who robbed a Fox charcoal merchant south of Shinden Kitsune; one has maho-cult scars on his forearms.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (20 koku): a former porter missing parts of two right-hand fingers who stole crates of lacquerware at the docks.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (20 koku): wreckers moving channel markers near Uminari north of Shiro Etsuko; one has a broken nose.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (20 koku): wanted for questioning by the Masao domain; expected at Kyuden Kakita for the Doll Festival.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (15 koku): Scorpion charcoal merchant who never paid the Fox for a shipment of white charcoal.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (15 koku): Flying Spears bandit from Aoyagi in the Reiji domain; big, nearly 6 feet, leans left from a hip injury.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (10 koku): a very polite con artist posing as a dignitary's advance man to cheat innkeepers in Etsuko and Kakita lands.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (10 koku): an attacker of Kakita Aichiko whose right ear she partially severed.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (5 koku): a rigged-dice cheat who escaped forced labor at Shiro Suzume; gap-toothed sleight-of-hand master.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: The lawful form of private vengeance: declared by those personally wronged against those who wronged them, it extends to every descendant of each named person's paternal great-grandfather on both sides, any of whom may lawfully kill any on the other side. Outsiders gain nothing from it.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Blood Feuds

summary: A messy all-hands Wasp job: delivering an Imperial summons to Ikoma Yuan at a teahouse ended with the Ikoma shugenja Ikoma Tsai killed. His father Ikoma Wataemon and brothers Ikoma Naohira and Ikoma Ietsugu declared a blood feud on the Wasp present, which reaches the PCs through their relatives; the three are on their way south. The source of the Righteous Sting and Venomous Sting advantage and disadvantage.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Family Reckoning

summary: Wasp campaign custom advantage: Family Reckoning advantage: your relative at the teahouse acted honorably; your Rank counts higher, and the party's too.

source.section: Custom advantages and disadvantages

summary: Wasp campaign custom disadvantage: Family Reckoning disadvantage: your relative at the teahouse acted questionably; your Rank counts lower, and the party's too.

source.section: Custom advantages and disadvantages

summary: Wasp campaign custom disadvantage: your household owes the Crane, who may ask you to advance their interests; refusing costs face.

source.section: Custom advantages and disadvantages

summary: Wasp campaign custom advantage: a letter of introduction from your lineage's chancellor; you count as higher Rank and Recognition with Wasp samurai.

source.section: Custom advantages and disadvantages

summary: Wasp campaign custom advantage: your household has real holdings, replacing Wealthy (every PC in this campaign is otherwise Poor).

source.section: Custom advantages and disadvantages

summary: Wasp campaign custom disadvantage: Imperial officials see you as a troublemaker from past bounties.

source.section: Custom advantages and disadvantages

summary: Wasp campaign custom disadvantage: the Zenji house (and the Matsu) hate you for past bounty work on Lion samurai.

source.section: Custom advantages and disadvantages

summary: Wasp campaign custom advantage: a strong ally in the Sparrow, Fox or Mantis, with clan-specific favors.

source.section: Custom advantages and disadvantages

summary: Wasp campaign custom disadvantage: you are the child of a peasant Tsuruchi raised to samurai; you are never of peer standing with samurai-born.

source.section: Custom advantages and disadvantages

summary: Wasp campaign custom disadvantage: Scorpion contacts sometimes ask you to thwart a fellow Wasp's egregious behavior.

source.section: Custom advantages and disadvantages

summary: Wasp campaign custom advantage: seasoned bounty-hunting experience; free raises on etiquette, law, intimidation and underworld rolls about your authority.

source.section: Custom advantages and disadvantages

summary: The Wasp campaign's own advantages and disadvantages: Crane-indebted, Family Reckoning (Righteous Sting / Venomous Sting), Highest Regard, Household wealth, Imperial disdain, Lion enmity, Minor Clan Major Ally, Peasantborn, Scorpion advocate, Streetwise.

source.section: Custom advantages and disadvantages

summary: The rules of the Measure of Standing for what is appropriate between samurai of different ranks, including when one samurai is of "peer standing" with another (merits such as advantages shift perceived rank). Governs bounties, duels and arrests. The campaign wiki has the full explanation.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Measure of Standing and the Accordances of Rank

summary: The bears of the Kitsune Mori (tsukinowaguma, "moon-ring bear"), black with a pale crescent on the chest. The worst is the anamotazu, "the one with no den", a bear that never denned and hunts hungry through winter.

source.section: Bears of the Kitsune Mori

summary: The system of government ministries formalized by Hantei the Tenth, repeated at the Imperial, Clan, Family, House and provincial levels: Rites, Revenue, Retainers, War, Works and Justice. The chancellery sets policy; the ministries carry it out.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government

summary: One of the Six Ministries, responsible for shrines, temples, festivals and religious obligations, and the registers of births, marriages and deaths. The Imperial Minister of Rites is also the High Priestess of Amaterasu and decides which doctrines are heresy.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > Ministry of Rites

summary: One of the Six Ministries, responsible for land taxes, business licenses and city-gate import tariffs. The Imperial Minister of Revenue is also called the Imperial Treasurer.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > Ministry of Revenue

summary: One of the Six Ministries, responsible for samurai stipends, ranks, civil service exams and promotions. The Imperial ministry also awards honors and commendations.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > Ministry of Retainers

summary: One of the Six Ministries, responsible for armies, weapons, armor, horses and maps. The Imperial Minister of War is the Shogun and oversees the Imperial legions.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > Ministry of War

summary: One of the Six Ministries, responsible for roads, walls, harbors, granaries and other public works, using corvee labor. At the Imperial level it also maintains the Kaiu Wall and the Imperial roads' waystations.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > Ministry of Works

summary: One of the Six Ministries, responsible for policing, bandit patrols, magistrates, courts and jails. The Imperial Minister of Justice is the Emerald Champion.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > Ministry of Justice

summary: The council that sets policy, made up of chancellors who represent lineages (at the House level) or houses (at the Imperial level). The Imperial chancellery advises the Emperor and in practice decides most matters; the Three Man Alliance votes there as a bloc.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government

summary: Head of the Imperial chancellery, of the 14th rank; currently Kakita Yoshi, who backed the creation of the Wasp Clan.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government

summary: The Imperial Chancellor, a Crane, who showed Tsuruchi his uncle's treacherous letter, promised Crane backing and arranged the Wasp Clan's charter.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Tsuruchi's revenge

summary: The title of the Imperial Minister of War, who oversees the Imperial legions.

summary: The title of the Imperial Minister of Revenue.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > The Ministry of War

summary: The title of the Imperial Minister of Justice, chosen by a dueling tournament to be the best duelist in the Empire and duel on the Emperor's behalf.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > The Ministry of Justice

summary: The title of the Imperial Minister of Rites.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > The Ministry of War

summary: The Emperor's magistrate in each domain, under the Emerald Charter: handles disputes between samurai of different clans, Imperial tax collection and legion recruiting, and registers and pays out Imperial bounties. Has a large staff of Imperial yoriki. Each of the six domains the PCs oversee has one.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > The Ministry of Justice

summary: An assistant to a magistrate (or official). The PCs are Tsuruchi Kyoma's yoriki; Tsuruchi began with former retainers as his yoriki.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > The Ministry of Justice

summary: The 15 ranks of the samurai caste: 15 the Emperor; 14 the Imperial Chancellor and the Clan daimyo; 13 Family daimyo and Imperial Ministers; 12 House daimyo; 11 Chancellor; 10 Minister; 9 Deputy Minister; 8 Governor; 7 Provincial Minister; 6 Deputy Provincial Minister; 5 County Magistrate; 4 Squad Sergeant; 3 Corporal; 2 legionnaire; 1 unposted samurai. Each rank has an upper and lower level (7.5 is "the upper seventh rank").

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government

summary: The lord of a Clan, Family or House (ranks 14, 13 and 12).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: A provincial governor (rank 8), who lives in the provincial city.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: Head of one of the six ministries at the provincial level (rank 7).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: The official administering a county from its town (rank 5).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: The peasant who oversees a village district from its main village.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: The steward of a household or official's staff.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: The servant who manages a samurai's household affairs.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: A level of the hierarchy: the largest grouping: the 7 Great Clans and the minor clans.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: A level of the hierarchy: each Great Clan has 3-5 Great Families, one of them ruling.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: A level of the hierarchy: a Family's ruling house or vassal house, each ruling one domain.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: A level of the hierarchy: a political coalition of samurai tracing to a notable ancestor; lineages with enough members sit on their house's chancellery.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: A level of the hierarchy: the land a House rules, about 70 miles across, usually about six provinces.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: A level of the hierarchy: part of a domain overseen by a Governor from the provincial city; about six counties.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: A level of the hierarchy: part of a province run by a County Magistrate from its town.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: A level of the hierarchy: part of a county overseen by a peasant Village Headsman, with outlying hamlets.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: The days of labor service every peasant household owes each year for roads, walls, dykes and other public works, called by the Ministry of Works.

summary: The anti-corruption rule at city gates: a sashed tariff inspector assesses goods but never touches money, and a licensor collects the posted rate without discretion.

Each Great Clan has two as its patrons: Crab Bishamon and Ebisu; Crane Benten and Daikoku; Dragon Hotei and Ebisu; Lion Bishamon and Daikoku; Phoenix Fukurokujin and Hotei; Scorpion Benten and Jurojin; Unicorn Fukurokujin and Jurojin.
